thought.text: Public tests pass. The fix is minimal and targeted: `has_select_fields` now also considers `self.annotations`, so when `alias()` moves an annotation out of the select mask, `RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup` no longer wrongly clears the select clause and re-adds only the target field while leaving annotations in place.

action.message:
Fixed the bug where `__in` didn't clear selected fields on the RHS when `QuerySet.alias()` was used after `annotate()`.

Root cause: `Query.has_select_fields` only checked `self.select`, `self.annotation_select_mask`, and `self.extra_select_mask`. When `alias()` is called after `annotate()`, the annotation is moved into `self.annotations` but removed from `annotation_select_mask`, so `has_select_fields` returned False. `RelatedIn.get_prep_lookup` then took the branch that calls `clear_select_clause()` and re-adds only the target field, but the annotations remained in `self.annotations`, producing a subquery with many columns ("sub-select returns 10 columns - expected 1").

Change (django/db/models/sql/query.py): `has_select_fields` now also returns True when `self.annotations` is non-empty, so the RHS select clause is properly cleared/replaced.

Verification: scoped public regression tests (annotations) pass — 80 tests, 0 failures.
